title: AI in Education 2026: Benefits, Risks, and What Parents Should Know
seoTitle: AI in Education 2026: Benefits, Risks & India Rules
excerpt: How AI tutors and marking tools work in 2026, CBSE's new AI syllabus, India's parental consent rules for kids' data, and what AI study tools cost in ₹.
content:
Quick note for readers outside India: the costs here are in Indian rupees (₹) and the rules section starts with India. If you're in the US, UK or EU, skip to the sections on your country. The advice on safety and privacy applies everywhere.

What Is AI in Education?

AI in education means software that uses machine learning to help people teach and learn. In 2026 that covers chatbot tutors, adaptive quizzes, automatic marking, lesson-planning assistants and speech or translation tools. Use is now close to universal among older students. The Higher Education Policy Institute's Student Generative AI Survey 2026, published on 12 March 2026, found that 95% of full-time UK undergraduates use AI in at least one way and 94% use it to help with assessed work. India has no national survey on the same scale, but Indian students use the same tools: ChatGPT, Gemini and the AI features built into exam-prep apps.

How Is AI Used in Classrooms Today?

Schools, coaching centres and students at home use AI in a few practical ways:

  • Adaptive practice: quiz platforms raise or lower question difficulty based on each answer, so a struggling student gets more practice and a quick learner moves on.
  • Chatbot tutors: general assistants such as ChatGPT and Gemini explain concepts and walk through problems at any hour.
  • Marking and feedback: teachers use AI to check multiple-choice tests and draft feedback, then review it themselves.
  • Lesson planning: AI drafts worksheets, quizzes and activities that a teacher then edits.
  • Access tools: speech-to-text, read-aloud and translation help students with dyslexia or hearing loss, and those studying in a second language.

In India, AI-generated practice questions are now common in JEE and NEET preparation. In England, the Department for Education says teachers can use AI for planning, resources and marking, but must check what it produces. In the US, federal guidance encourages AI for tutoring and teacher support while keeping teachers in charge.

What Are the Benefits of AI in Education?

The biggest benefit is personal attention at scale. A class of 40, or a coaching batch of 150, can't give every student one-to-one help. An AI tutor can at least answer each student's own question at their own pace. For students in towns without good private tutors, that matters.

AI also saves teachers time. Drafting a worksheet or a set of practice questions takes minutes instead of an hour, which leaves more time for actual teaching. And access tools help students who were often left behind: a child with dyslexia can listen to a chapter, and a student who thinks in Odia or Tamil can get an English explanation translated.

What Are the Risks of AI in Education?

Wrong answers. AI tools still make confident mistakes, especially in maths, recent events and local syllabus details. A student who doesn't check can learn something false.

Copying instead of learning. HEPI's 2026 survey found that 12% of UK undergraduates put AI-generated text directly into assessed work, up from 8% in 2025 and 3% in 2024. Students who let AI do the thinking struggle in exams where AI isn't allowed.

Privacy. Learning apps collect a lot: answers, time spent, voice recordings and sometimes location. For children, that data is sensitive, and India's new data law treats it that way (see below).

A wider gap. Families who can pay for premium plans get more powerful tools, while others use free tiers with lower limits and, in some cases, ads.

What Are the Rules in India?

AI is now part of the school syllabus. According to the Ministry of Education's written reply in the Rajya Sabha on 5 August 2026, NCERT and CBSE introduced a Computational Thinking and Artificial Intelligence curriculum for Classes 3 to 8 from the 2026-27 academic year. The curriculum for Classes 9 to 12 has been finalised. CBSE's CT and AI page carries the syllabus and the student and teacher resource books. The same reply describes SOAR (Skilling for AI Readiness), a Ministry of Skill Development programme with three 15-hour AI modules for students in Classes 6 to 12 and a 45-hour module for teachers.

Children's data needs a parent's consent. The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 were notified in November 2025. Under the DPDP Act, anyone under 18 is a child. Rule 10 says a company must get verifiable consent from a parent before processing a child's personal data, and must check that the person consenting is an identifiable adult. A government press release of 12 December 2025 applies this directly to digital education platforms. It also notes an exemption that lets schools track and monitor students for educational activities and safety. These child-data duties take effect 18 months after the Rules were published, which works out to 13 May 2027.

What this means for parents: from May 2027, an edtech app should ask you, not your child, before collecting your child's data. If an app lets a 14-year-old sign up with no parent check, treat that as a warning sign today.

What Are the Rules in the US, UK and EU?

United States: on 22 July 2025 the U.S. Department of Education sent a Dear Colleague letter on using federal grant funds for AI. It says AI can be used for tutoring, teacher support and other functions under existing programmes, as long as the uses follow the law and keep educators in their role. Student records handled by AI tools are still covered by FERPA.

United Kingdom: the Department for Education's Generative AI in education guidance (first published 29 March 2023, last updated 12 August 2025, applies to England) leaves most decisions to schools. They must protect pupil data, follow safeguarding rules, and teachers stay responsible for anything AI produces.

European Union: the EU AI Act lists education as a high-risk area in Annex III. That covers AI used to decide admissions, evaluate learning outcomes, set the level of education a student gets, and monitor students for cheating during tests. These systems face stricter rules on transparency, data and human oversight.

How Much Do AI Study Tools Cost in India?

Most students don't need a special edtech subscription to use AI. The main general-purpose assistants have free tiers, and the paid plans below are what most families would actually consider. Prices were checked on 23 November 2026 and can change.

ToolPrice in IndiaNotes
ChatGPT Free / Gemini free₹0Enough for most homework help; lower usage limits
ChatGPT Go₹399 a monthOpenAI's standard India price; the free-year offer is closed to new users
Google AI Plus₹399 a monthGoogle One India price; free for 12 months for eligible college students who redeem by 31 December 2026
Google AI Pro₹1,950 a monthHigher limits and 5 TB storage; discounted student bundles available
DIKSHA₹0Government platform with free NCERT-aligned content

For a household, the maths is simple. One ₹399 plan costs ₹4,788 a year. If two children each want their own, that's ₹9,576 a year. Before paying, check whether your child's school or college already provides access. Also check the student offer: Google's student offer for India gives eligible college students aged 18 or over a free year of AI Plus, but it needs a payment method at sign-up and renews automatically unless cancelled.

Where Else Is AI in Education Growing?

Singapore, South Korea and China have national plans to bring AI into schools, and the EU is building rules around it. UNICEF's policy guidance on AI for children sets out child-rights principles that many governments refer to, including privacy, safety, fairness and explainability. Across the world, the debate has moved from whether students use AI to how to make them use it well.

What Safety Precautions Should Parents and Students Follow?

  • Check answers. Compare AI explanations with the NCERT textbook or your teacher's notes, especially in maths and science.
  • Use it to learn, not to finish. Ask the AI to explain a step or quiz you, not to write the whole answer.
  • Read the privacy policy. Avoid apps that ask for location, contacts or photos without a clear reason.
  • Use a parent's account for under-18s where the app allows it, and keep personal details such as school name and address out of chats.
  • Watch auto-renewals. Free trials often renew at full price; set a reminder a few days before the end date.

Conclusion

AI is already inside Indian classrooms. CBSE is teaching it from Class 3, and India's data law will soon require parental consent before apps collect children's data. Used well, AI gives students patient, personal help and gives teachers back time. Used badly, it hands out wrong answers, invites copying and collects more data than it should. Treat it as a study partner that needs checking, keep a parent in the loop for younger students, and pay only for what a free tier can't do.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can AI replace teachers?

No. AI can help with practice questions, marking and planning, but both the UK and US guidance keep teachers responsible for teaching and assessment.

Is AI in education safe for children?

It can be, with adult supervision and apps that protect data. In India, apps will need verifiable parental consent before processing a child's data once the DPDP Rules' child-data duties apply from 13 May 2027.

Are AI study tools free in India?

The free tiers of ChatGPT and Gemini cover most homework help, and DIKSHA is free. Paid plans start at ₹399 a month.

Is AI taught in Indian schools?

Yes. CBSE schools teach Computational Thinking and AI in Classes 3 to 8 from the 2026-27 academic year.

Will AI make homework obsolete?

No. Homework still checks understanding, and exams are still taken without AI. Students who copy AI answers fall behind when it counts.

How do I know if an AI education app is safe?

Look for a clear privacy policy, a parent sign-up step for under-18s, no requests for unnecessary permissions, and a way to delete your child's data.
